notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); no hardware was attached, no hardware backend and no MuJoCo engine or upstream environment was run. The card's entry symbols exist and are concrete: envs.h1.h1_env:H1Env at envs/h1/h1_env.py:11 and envs.jvrc.jvrc_walk:JvrcWalkEnv at envs/jvrc/jvrc_walk.py:13. The package serves the card's models[0], models/jvrc_mj_description/xml/scene.xml, through the card's MujocoDriver family; the scene includes jvrc1.xml. NOT COVERED: the JvrcWalkEnv environment layer (its reduced generated XML, action smoothing, PD control, observation history, clock and mode observations, reward and termination); this driver exposes the raw MJCF control vector, not the environment's policy action. The loaded model has one free root joint plus 44 hinges (51 qpos, 50 qvel) and 34 motors; those dimensions are derived by the fake from the MJCF text, not hard-coded. MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs (no network, no pip), so fake.py is a stand-in mujoco module: it parses the MJCF for the joint layout, actuator targets and option timestep but integrates a placeholder first-order motion and resolves no mesh, contact, equality, tendon or sensor; it was never compared with the real engine. The sim path (a backend name that backends does not list, which imports the real mujoco) was not run. No control bound is invented: the jvrc1 default motor class sets ctrllimited=false and forcelimited=false (models/jvrc_mj_description/xml/jvrc1.xml:10-13) and no motor declares a ctrlrange, so the bridge publishes action.ctrl as operator_required and refuses a step that sets it until site-limits.json supplies a bound; site-limits.example.json is operator example data (an illustrative interval, source operator, reason starts 'example only:'), not a model value or a deployment bound. Expected warnings: G1.SUBMODULE_SOURCE (the jvrc_mj_description submodule is read at its gitlink bfb2bf25966ddfe0d0248385ef7e2586963c86a0; the card does not state the submodule licence), G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND (the fake is a stand-in library object, not a recorded native surface), and G8.NO_UNIT x3 (bridge-derived ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed). No catalogue requests: only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are used. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package. The upstream clone was not modified.

MODEL REVIEW (gpt-6.1-sol, a model and not a human, 2026-11-17; reviewed_by stays null): Model review found a zero floating-base reset pose, qvel indexed with qpos addresses, and torque motors treated as position targets. fake.py now preserves model defaults including the unit root quaternion, uses separate velocity addresses and applies explicitly placeholder motor-driven acceleration; driver.py selects analytic F0 fidelity for this backend and records the omitted H1 task and the JVRC submodule licence. test_driver.py corrects reset/fidelity assertions and adds a motor-address/momentum regression; facts.md, reference.json and REFERENCE.md were synchronized, and check-report.json was regenerated. The fake gate and strict collector pass with contract_checked evidence; no upstream engine or hardware execution is claimed. For the human reviewer: The served device is the raw 34-motor JVRC1 scene, not JvrcWalkEnv or H1Env. action.ctrl requires an operator envelope; the example overlay is illustrative, and steps without an action retain controls. The model submodule at bfb2bf25966ddfe0d0248385ef7e2586963c86a0 has its own BSD-2-Clause LICENSE. G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND describe the gate path for a stand-in library object here, not an actual MuJoCo run; gravity, damping, coupled dynamics and contacts are omitted.
